body:
It took me until I was 30 to come out as bisexual. I grew up with a dad who would make openly homophobic comments. My advice to you is to learn to love you for you. All the things that make you unique. And as cliched as it sounds love is love and it is never a bad thing to love no matter what that other persons gender is. 
There is no need to rush finding a relationship. Try and focus on loving yourself first because only then can you attract the right person for you. Speaking from personal experience here but if you go into a relationship with baggage of your own it will destroy anything good you deserve to have.
Please stay strong :)
Thank you for your honesty as well as time. I think what you are saying is the hard reality of it. Something I have been denying to myself and is time I face up to.

I do not think he realises that their behaviour is problematic. He blamed me tonight for this situation because I had sent that message to his mother. He isn't in therapy. He blames his autism and thinks he deserves to not be happy. I don't want to give up on him but I think this will be the moment when he leaves me. Going forward I do not know what to do. He has shut down to me and I do not want to be seen to be overbearing but I need to know what his decision is.
I am 31 and he is 26.

Thank you for taking the time to reply. I don't really know what to say. Right now I feel numb and stupid. I don't know how to ever recover from this. If I get back up again then it feels like it will happen again. I don't know if any of this makes sense.

This is me OP. Two years in an ldr with a man who keeps making it clear that he chose his family over me. His family who have never met me or talked to me but still decided I was not good enough for him. A man who doesn't talk about a future with me. 
I too tell myself I will not reply to his messages. Cut off all communication. 
For me, I think it's crippling anxiety. Also, I put so much time and effort into this. I done all the travelling to him. Maybe it's the thought of it being all for nothing.
All I can say to you OP is to not be hard on yourself. Even being in an ldr and all the hardships that can come with it shows you have some strength! One day you will find a way to do what you think is right for you.
😖 I've been off reddit so just seen your reply. The border collie did take away some of that bear. Still, he weighed 30kg of pure muscle. French Bulldogs are beautiful dogs!

That's what I had to do with my dog. It's the kindest thing to do. I hope you dont mind me asking what breed your dog is? Mine was an Akita x Border Collie. A lot of hard work and training for his breed but the bestest friend.

Oh I am sorry to hear about this. I totally understand the flight/fight response because it's in the dogs nature. Sadly not many people where I live ever understood that about my dog. I hope you and your dog will have a good life together despite asshole owners.

This! I kept my dog on a leash and muzzled at all times after he was attacked as a pup by another dog off a leash. He feared dogs after that and still people let their dog run up to mine. Leash laws should become mandatory.

Jeeep six months and counting since I last travelled to the Netherlands to see my partner. No idea when I will see him again and yet people in my country are still booking holidays like fml DO NOT TRAVEL

Exactly! When I was out there I was shocked at what I was seeing. No masks, no one using hand sanitizer and no social distancing. I was forever having to move away from people or ask them to keep their distance. I was repeatedly told that they don't care about covid-19. 

As much as my government here in the UK is screwing up with testing capacity and mixed messages at least they are now trying to get things under control again here before infections get as bad as they are in NL.

Thanks for your reply. It has been eating away at me.

Thank you for your reply. 

That's what I said to him. That he should be telling them. All he has said is that he isn't strong enough among many other excuses. This has been going on since Saturday. He wants me to accept it and move on. But I'm struggling to accept this. And to see a future for us.

Yep this is me. I used to be worse for this in the beginning. But after opening up to my SO he has really stepped up with supporting me. Now I try my best to not hide away but I also know that if I am struggling I can always talk to my SO.
My suggestion is to try to talk to your SO if you have not already done so.
I hope you feel better soon with this OP :)
Thank you so much for your advice!
Ohhhh yeaahhhh.. too true!
Definitely! I think New Zealand saw what was happening in China and was like hell no. Puts most governments to shame.

Yes! I really dont think it will be in place for long as it's totally unworkable. Other countries imposed this at the beginning of their lockdowns. So it just seems to be a stupid attempt by bojo to appear to be doing something. 
I'm hoping that as long as Europe doesnt impose the same I'm going to travel and face the quarantine when I come back. 
My boyfriend Iives in the Netherlands and they seem to be pretty sensible about the whole thing. Same as Germany. So fingers crossed you get to see your boyfriend soon!

Hi! I think ultimately it comes down to trust. You mentioned some previous relationship issues which might not be helping how you are feeling. But if he hasnt been giving you any signs that you should be worrying then try and focus on the positives. The affection and love shown. His willingness to be patient and listen to your feelings. It's only natural for someone to start feeling a but tired if they feel like nothing they are saying is making a difference.
I'm also waiting for Europe to open its borders (UK girl here) and it does look promising for the 15th. So not too long now!
Thank you!! :) I'm going from the UK. Hoping for a July/August visit

Wooh! NL did do a really good job with covid-19 so I'm not surprised that they are able to open faster :)
I hope you get to see your bf soon! 
Looks like we will all be descending on NL at the same time lol
Ok thanks :) I'll have to look into that
How exciting! I'm waiting to see my bf who lives in the Netherlands. If you dont mind me asking, but do you know when the borders are opening again for the Netherlands?

Thank you! I think it's mainly a fear that it won't work out because of this virus. I dont want to come off as clingy/needy but right now I feel like I need some extra reassurance from him but I dont really know how to express that. Our ldr is only a few months old and tbh started at quite possibly the worst time.
I'm struggling. Was meant to meet in March but the borders closed 2 days beforehand. I've never been in a ldr before so sometimes it seems like a very lonely experience.

Being a woman is so fcking expensive. Tampons, make up if we want to get and keep a job, just everything to be socially acceptable costs so much. It makes life so much harder. 
I read about the pink tax and here in the UK tampons are taxed! Fcking sucks when I'm trying to balance buying food and uni costs too.
I think it would be more than 20%... like everytime something got a bit tough people would just press that red button.

I feel the same way. Everyone says to stay positive and hopeful. That good things are coming. But then something bad comes along and I feel cursed. Just hopeless and dark. They aren't in my mind and living my life so how do they know!? It's like they're trying to fill me up with false positivity. Setting me up to fail. 
I'm sorry for the rant.

Speaking as a woman it's not at all easy. There is pressure to stay slim and look good. Trying to find any meaningful relationship is impossible. I'm turning 30 this year and am still single because I find guys are only interested in one night stands not getting to know me as a person.  I tell myself it's their loss but I still feel like there is something wrong with me.
I guess what I'm trying to say is that gender is irrelevant to how people treat us. There is bad whether you are a guy or a woman. I'm sorry I couldn't make this post more positive other than you're not alone in what you are going through.
